title.rendered: Lo, I Am With You Always: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age.” A morning devotional on the promise that carries you into every tomorrow.

content.rendered:
A mountain in Galilee. The risen Christ. Eleven men who had watched Him die and eaten breakfast with Him alive again. The last words Jesus spoke on earth before ascending to the Father. Words the Church has been walking in ever since.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, September 19, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, ‘All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.’ Amen.”
Matthew 28:18-20 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

A mountain in Galilee, not named by Matthew, sometime in the forty days between the resurrection and the ascension. The risen Christ stood on that mountain with eleven men who had watched Him die on Friday and eaten breakfast with Him alive again on Sunday. They worshipped Him. Matthew, honest as always, adds that some doubted. The men who followed Him for three years, watched Him crucified, seen the empty tomb, touched the scars, still had lingering questions. And Jesus, without addressing the doubts, spoke words that have echoed down twenty centuries of Christian history. It was His last recorded speech on earth before ascending to the Father. What He said is often called the Great Commission, but the last sentence of it may be the most personal of all.

“All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Jesus opens with authority. He does not send the eleven with encouragement. He sends them with authority. His authority, delegated to them, sufficient for the impossible task He is about to place on their shoulders. Then the assignment. Go. Make disciples. Baptise. Teach. Not just of Israel. Of all the nations. Not just a project for this generation. A movement for every generation until He returns.

Then the promise. And this is the sentence that has carried more believers through more hard seasons than perhaps any other in the whole New Testament. “Lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Not, “I will send angels to help you.” Not, “I will send My Spirit and then withdraw.” Jesus Himself, personally, would be with them. Always. To the end of the age. The Greek phrase is egō meth’ hymōn eimi pasas tas hēmeras heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos. Every one of those words carries weight. I. With you. Am. All the days. Until the completion of the age.

The Passion Translation captures the promise with striking depth: “And I will be with you always, to the very end of the age” (Matthew 28:20 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And behold, I am with you all the days (perpetually, uniformly, and on every occasion), to the [very] close and consummation of the age. Amen (so let it be)” (Matthew 28:20 AMPC). Perpetually. Uniformly. On every occasion. The last five words of Jesus’ earthly ministry are the promise the Church has walked in on every mission field, in every persecution, through every plague, in every hard season for two thousand years. He is with us. All the days. Uniformly. On every occasion.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this closes our September walk through the Gospels. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, whatever mountain you are standing on this morning, whatever mission the risen Christ has placed on your life, whatever you are being sent into this coming week, take the last sentence of Jesus’ earthly ministry with you. He goes with you. Not to send you out and then withdraw. Not to give you the assignment and then leave you to it. With you. All the days. Every day. Every mission field is His. Every ordinary Monday is His. Every hard season is His. And the same Jesus who spoke those words on the mountain in Galilee is speaking them personally over your life today. Lo, I am with you always. Even to the end of the age.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus goes with me. Not just at conversion. Not just in the church building. Always. All the days. To every mountain I climb this week. To every mission You have placed on my life. To every ordinary Monday and every hard season. He is with me. His authority accompanies me. His presence sustains me. His promise anchors me. Whatever You are sending me into next, I go with the assurance of the last sentence Jesus ever spoke on earth. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus is with me always, even to the end of the age. His authority accompanies me. His presence sustains me. I go into every day this week with the risen Christ.

  • Acts 1:8 (NKJV): You shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you
